en: The Sūtra on the Teaching of Generosity,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Rank of Chao San Da Fu, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master Mingjiao, the Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, where he was teaching the Dharma of giving to a great assembly of bhikṣus.
There are thirty-seven kinds:
First, by practicing generosity with faith and reverence, one shall become free from all envy and be honored and revered by others;
second, by giving at the proper time, one attains purity of the three karmas and peace and security throughout the four seasons;
third, by practicing generosity constantly, one attains physical and mental well-being and freedom from distraction or loss.
Fourth, by giving with one's own hands, one attains long and slender fingers and a well-proportioned physical form;
fifth, by giving for the sake of others, one further causes others to practice great renunciation and generosity;
sixth, by giving in accordance with the teachings, the mind remains free from grasping at signs, thereby attaining unconditioned merit.
Seventh, by giving gifts of exquisite forms, one obtains a physical appearance that is dignified and handsome, becoming an object of affection for all;
eighth, by giving gifts of superior and wonderful fragrances, one constantly attains the scent of sandalwood and enjoys its offerings;
ninth, by giving gifts of superior flavors, one obtains the most excellent of flavors, which nourishes and benefits the limbs.
10. By giving with respect in accordance with the Dharma, one attains peace and happiness, and is joyfully beheld by all people;
11. By giving with a vast mind, one attains immeasurable and expansive merit;
12. By giving delicious food, one attains freedom from famine, and one's granaries and treasuries overflow.
Thirteen: By giving drinks, one attains freedom from hunger and thirst wherever one goes;
fourteen: by giving clothing, one obtains exquisite garments that adorn the physical form;
fifteen: by giving dwellings, one obtains spacious fields and houses, adorned with multi-storied pavilions.
Sixteenth, by giving bedding and seating, one is born into a noble family with radiant and pure requisites;
seventeenth, by giving elephants, horses, chariots, and palanquins, one attains the four bases of psychic power and their unimpeded, wondrous application;
eighteenth, by giving medicinal decoctions, one attains peace and happiness, free from all diseases.
19. By giving the gift of the Dharma through the sūtras, one attains the supernormal powers such as the recollection of past lives;
20. By giving flowers and fruits, one attains the flowers of the seven factors of enlightenment;
21. By giving flower garlands, one attains liberation from the defilements of greed, hatred, and delusion.
Twenty-second: By giving incense as a gift, one attains freedom from the foul stench of afflictions;
twenty-third: by giving parasols and canopies as gifts, one attains mastery over the Dharma;
twenty-fourth: by giving bells and chimes as gifts, one attains exquisite and beautiful speech and voice.
Twenty-fifth, by giving the gift of music, one obtains a Brahma-voice that is profound and wondrous;
twenty-sixth, by giving the gift of lighting lamps, one obtains the purity of the divine eye;
twenty-seventh, by giving the gift of silks and fine fabrics, one obtains the garments of liberation.
28. Sprinkling fragrant water upon the stūpas and temples of the Tathāgata;
29. Bathing the body of the Tathāgata with fragrant water; 30.
Anointing and adorning the images of the Buddha with fragrant oil—by these, one attains the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics.
31. By giving scented water for the bathing of the Sangha, one is born into a wealthy and noble family, with little illness and great peace and happiness;
32. By giving with a mind of loving-kindness, one obtains a serene and pleasant countenance, free from all anger and resentment;
33. By giving with a mind of compassion, one attains freedom from killing and harming.
34. By giving with a joyful mind, one attains fearlessness and remains far removed from sorrow and affliction;
35. By giving with an equanimous mind, one attains freedom from obstruction and realizes the bliss of nirvana;
36. By giving various kinds of gifts, one attains various kinds of merit.
Thirty-seven: By practicing giving with a mind that is non-abiding and signless, one attains unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"These thirty-seven kinds are the practices of the wise."
"This subtle and wondrous practice, you should now receive and uphold.
At that time, the King of Śrāvastī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"How should we, then, practice giving?
The Buddha said, "Great King!"
When practicing giving with the aim of seeking superior and wondrous merit and retribution, one should refrain from killing with a heart of loving-kindness, remain free from all envy and jealousy;
be endowed with right view, stay far from unwholesome states,
firmly uphold the prohibitive precepts, and draw near to virtuous friends.
It closes the gates to the evil realms and opens the path to rebirth in the heavens;
it benefits both oneself and others with an impartial mind.
To give in such a manner is true giving and constitutes a great field of merit.
Furthermore, by practicing generosity according to one's own wishes, one obtains its corresponding retribution.

If one personally bestows gifts of exquisite form, renowned fragrance, rare flavors, or soft textures, one will obtain the retribution of being respected by all people, having a complete circle of kinsmen, and enjoying wealth, nobility, peace, and happiness;
or if one bestows food and drink, one will obtain great strength.
By giving lamps of ghee and oil as an offering, one attains the divine eye;
by giving music as an offering, one attains the divine ear;
and by giving medicinal decoctions as an offering, one attains long life.
"By giving dwellings as a gift, one obtains multi-storied pavilions and fields;
by giving the teaching of the Dharma as a gift, one obtains the nectar of immortality.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
“Great King! If one practices the ten wholesome actions as an act of giving, one further obtains ten kinds of retributions. The ten wholesome actions are:

abstaining from killing, abstaining from stealing, abstaining from sexual misconduct, abstaining from false speech, abstaining from frivolous speech, abstaining from harsh speech, abstaining from divisive speech, abstaining from covetousness, abstaining from ill will, and abstaining from delusion. By these, one obtains: a life not cut short prematurely; wealth that does not dissipate; a pure retinue; words that are truthful and sincere; freedom from all envy; being pleasing to others to behold; harmony among friends and relatives; not falling into poverty or low status; a handsome and upright countenance; and being endowed with wisdom.”
"Such is the retribution one receives.
The Buddha said, "Great King!"
If one makes offerings of the most excellent food and drink to the Triple Gem, one shall obtain five kinds of benefits:
a dignified and handsome physical appearance, increased vigor and strength, an extended lifespan, happiness and tranquility, and the accomplishment of eloquence.

In this way, for all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa—whether parents, wives, children, or male and female relatives—their aspirations and requests were fully realized through such acts of giving, leaving nothing unfulfilled.
When he had spoken this Dharma, they were all greatly rejoiced; they paid homage and withdrew.
The Sūtra on Generosity Spoken by the Buddha.
